content_units: Birthday Karaoke Flow

A 15-song set should start easy, lift the room in waves, and save the biggest communal choruses for the middle and final stretch. This lineup is built for guests 25–55, with familiar songs from the 70s–2010s and amateur-friendly vocal ranges.
15-Song Karaoke Set List
Song   Artist   Decade   Energy   Vocal Difficulty   Singalong Moment
1   I Wanna Dance with Somebody   Whitney Houston   1980s   High   Medium   Early room-opener; everyone knows the chorus
2   Wonderwall   Oasis   1990s   Low   Easy   Cool-down reset; strong group chorus
3   Valerie   Mark Ronson ft. Amy Winehouse   2000s   Medium   Easy   Keeps momentum without straining voices
4   Sweet Caroline   Neil Diamond   1960s   Medium   Easy     Big singalong  1   — “ba ba ba” lands perfectly here
5   Shake It Off   Taylor Swift   2010s   High   Easy   High-energy bounce, very low vocal risk
6   Stand by Me   Ben E. King   1960s   Low   Easy   Gentle reset; good for mixed-confidence singers
7   Dancing Queen   ABBA   1970s   High   Medium     Big singalong  2   — broad age-range appeal
8   Mr. Brightside   The Killers   2000s   High   Medium   Peak crowd participation without being vocally brutal
9   No Scrubs   TLC   1990s   Low   Medium   Groove break; keeps variety and nostalgia high
10   Livin' on a Prayer   Bon Jovi   1980s   High   Medium-Hard     Big singalong  3   — place after a breather so the room is ready
11   Hey Jude   The Beatles   1960s   Low-Medium   Easy   Massive communal “na-na-na” moment without burnout
12   Uptown Funk   Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars   2010s   High   Medium   Dance spike; better for charismatic than perfect singers
13   Don't Stop Believin'   Journey   1980s   Medium-High   Medium     Big singalong  4   — late-set emotional lift
14   Flowers   Miley Cyrus   2020s   Low-Medium   Easy   Modern cooldown before the finale
15   Bohemian Rhapsody   Queen   1970s   High   Medium-Hard     Finale singalong   — theatrical closer, everyone joins in
Singalong Placement Strategy
-   Song 4 — Sweet Caroline:   first big shared moment, early enough to hook the room.
-   Song 7 — Dancing Queen:   cross-generational sweet spot; lifts the party again.
-   Song 10 — Livin' on a Prayer:   best placed after lower-energy songs so it feels huge.
-   Song 13 — Don't Stop Believin':   late emotional peak when the room is fully warmed up.
-   Song 15 — Bohemian Rhapsody:   finale closer for maximum group chaos and fun.
Host Notes for Smooth Energy Control
- Put   confident singers   on songs 1, 7, 10, 13, and 15.
- Use songs 2, 6, 11, and 14 as   recovery slots   for both voices and attention span.
- If the crowd gets louder than expected, swap song 14 and 15 for a harder finish.
- If the room is shy, move   Sweet Caroline   to slot 3 and   Valerie   to slot 4.
